purpose: answer-key study of the released wide-field (jupiter-auroras2) BEFORE v2 tuning — staged reference files + measured display-domain hue/level anchors the balance ladder aims at (the user's eyes remain the judge)

files.jupiter-auroras2_original.tif: 3283x2829 RGBA LZW — the live full-res original (esawebb.org/media/archives/images/original/jupiter-auroras2.tif; the cdn.../original path 404s)

staged.note: NASA-side full-res originals of the Aug-2022 deliverables are dead links since the blogs.nasa.gov migration (only 1024px renditions survive); ESA hosts the only live originals. SVS 31191 carries 3840x2160 presentation PNGs incl. a false-color variant.

visual_study_widefield: disc carries FULL band detail (belts, zones, GRS as pale oval, turbulence) — mid-tone, NOT blown; EZ cream ~77% display, belts ~40%
cyan is CONFINED to polar aurora glow + limb rim (exactly where our F335M NaN saturation crescents sit — the open policy point renders THERE in the original as bright cyan)
ring thin and neutral-gray with brighter ansae; Amalthea a spiked point at the left ansa; Adrastea fainter
large soft NEUTRAL diffraction fans below/around the disc are KEPT, not clipped
sky near-black but lifted (~10/255), faint galaxies + stars present
release canvas 3283x2829 (aspect 1.16) vs our full f212n grid 4340x4319 (1.00) — the release is a CROP/framing choice; framing is the user's call at judge time

reference_hue_anchors_rgb_0_255.method: 13x13 median windows at hand-placed points on the original TIFF (diagnostic sampling; display-domain)

craft_reading: the caption's 'orange vs cyan' lands as a RESTRAINED duotone: disc warm by only ~10% in R:G:B ratio, aurora ~28% blue-excess; ring/sky/spikes exactly neutral — naive saturated colorize weights overshoot the reference by a wide margin
matches Schmidt's stated policy 'I try to get it to look natural' (NASA blog)
sky pedestal lifted, not crushed — the deep arm's black point must not clip to 0
